ANNOUCEMENT BY THE CHAIRMAN 
Mr. Chairman: Hon. Members, based on the notice given by Dr. 
Manmohan Singh and others, I have admitted the following motion, under 
Rule 170 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Rajya Sabha: 
"That this House expresses deep anguish at the persistence of violence in 
Gujarat for over six weeks leading to loss of lives of a large number of 
persons, destruction of property worth crores of rupees, and urges the 
Central Government to intervene effectively under article 355 of the 
Constitution to protect the lives and properties of the citizens and to 
provide effective relief and rehabilitation to the victims of violence." 
The discussion will take place on Thursday, the 2nd May, 2002.

Scarcity in Secunderabad Cantonment Board area 
*441.   SHRI K: KALAVENKATA RAO :† 
        DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR: 
Will the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a severe water crisis in the Secunderabad 
Cantonment Board area; 
(b) if so, the reasons for irregularities in water supply in the Cantonment 
area; and 
(c) the action proposed to solve the water problem there? 
† The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Shri K. Kalavenkata Rao. 
 
1

RAJYA SABHA [24 April, 2002] 
.THE MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES): (a) to 
(c) A"Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
Water to the Cantonment area is supplied by Hyderabad Metropolitan 
Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB). Owing to repairs undertaken 
by HMWSSB of the main water pipe line and damages to their pumping system 
there was disruption in regular water su pply which resulted in water scarcity 
problem not only to the Cantonment area in other areas of twin cities of 
Secunderabad and Hyderabad. 
Secunderabad Cantonment Board has handed over a sum of Rs.63.32 
lakhs towards connection charges to HMWSSB for increasing the qunatum of 
bulk water supply from 27 lakhs gallons per day to 37 lakh gallons per day 
which will commence shortly. Cantonmet Board is also executing a project for 
laying new distribution pipe lines to benefit 50 Housing colonies apart from 
digging 25 deep bore wells. This has been done in addition to the existing 110 
electric bore wells and 700 hand pump bore wells for water supply to the 
residents of Cantonment area. This will mitigate the severe shortage of water to 
a large extent 
SHRI K. KALAVENKATA RAO: Sir, the population of Secunderabad 
Cantonment Board area is more than th ree lakhs. The people are facing great 
problems due to shortage of water supply, and the water that is supplied is very 
dirty. The water mains are very old, and, as a result, water from the sewer lines 
gets mixed up with the drinking water. What steps is the Government taking for 
ensuring adequate supply of clean water to the civilians and the people in the 
Cantonment Board area of Secunderabad? 
SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES: Sir, there is, essentially, shortage of water 
in Hyderabad and Secunderabad areas. The Cantonment Board gets its water 
supply from the Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board, 
just as in the case of the twin cities. Now, the shortage of water supply is due to 
reasons that are beyond the control of anyone. The Cantonment Board has 
taken a lot of action to overcome this problem, in so far as the 2.5 lakh population 
of the Cantonment itself is concerned. What they have tried to do is, one, they 
are executing a new project costing Rs.8 4 lakhs, where they are laying new 
distribution lines from the Karkhana Reservoir up to the Jupiter Colony. I am

15 housing colonies, from Govindpalli to the Park View Colony, and it will

area.

WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS 
Meetings of Inter-State Council 
* 444. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of meeting Inter-State Council held during the last year; 
(b) the subjects which were discussed and the recommendations made; 
(c) the details of recommendations which are yet to be implemented; 
(d) if so, by when those recommendations will be implemented; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI I.D. SWAMI): (a) The seventh meeting of the Inter-State Council was 
held on the 16th November, 2001 in New Delhi. 
(b) In this meeting, 59 recommendations contained in the report of 
Sarkaria Commission on various subjects viz, Legislative Relations, Role of 
Governor, All India Services, Inter-Governmental Council, Mines and Minerals, 
Mass Media etc. were considered. Some of the important recommendations 
made by the Council include the following:— 
(i) All residuary powers of legislation including those of taxation 
matters should be transferred from the Union List to the Concurrent 
List in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution. 
(ii) For legislation in respect of subjects in the Concurrent List, there 
should be active consultation with the State Governments except in 
emergent cases. 
(iii) A comprehensive Central legislation should be brought up in regard 
to imposition of taxes by the local bodies on the properties of the 
Union Government, which are of industrial and commercial nature. 
(iv) Consultation with the State Chief Ministers in the selection of a 
person to be appointed as Governor should be made obligatory 
. through a Constitutional amendment. 
(c) to (e) Of the 59 recommendations of the Sarkaria Commission 
considered in the meeting held on the 16th of November, 2001, the Inter-State 
26 

[24 April, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
Council recommended acceptance of 40 recommendations and the remaining 
19 were recommended for rejection. The recommendations of the Inter-State 
Council have been forwarded to the concerned Ministries and State Governments 
in January, 2002 for implementation. The major recommendations regarding 
legislative relations, role of Governors etc. would, if accepted by the Government, 
require amendments to the Constitution. Many of the aspects covered by the 
above recommendations of the Sarkaria Commission/Inter-State Council have 
also been examined by the National Commission set up to Review the Working 
of Constitution and they have given their recommendations. The Government 
will need to take a comprehensive view on these issues after examining the 
recommendations of the Inter-State Council as well as the Constitution Review 
Commission. Therefore, it is not possible to indicate a definite time-frame by

THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SURESH PRABHU): (a) to (d) The 
Government of India has been providing financial assistance in the form of 
additional Central Plan Assistance und er Accelerated Power Development 
Programme (APDP) to bring about necessary reforms in the State Power Sector 
for it to achieve commercial viability. The Ministry of Finance had provided 
Rs. 1000 crores and Rs. 1500 crores in the FY 2000-01 and FY 2001-02

bring about the desired efficiency in the distribution sector. Initially 
36 

[24 April, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
63 distribution circles all over the country have been taken up for development 
as Centre of Excellence with the objectives of reducing T&D (technical as well 
as commercial) losses to 10-15 per cent as against existing over 50 per cent; 
improving quality and reliability of power supply and customer satisfaction 
through investment in upgradation of sub-transmission and distribution network. 
It is proposed to take up all the circles in the country for upgradation of sub-
transmission and distribution network during the 10th Plan. APDP is being 
used as a tool to engineer reforms in the distribution sector, which is crucial to 
bringing commercial viability of the power sector, given in the fact that over 
75 per cent of total T&D losses take place at distribution stage. Distribution 
reform will bring about financial viability to the power sector to enable it to 
sustain investment in the sector.

replacement/installation of distribution transforms and reconductoring have 
been sanctioned which would help in improvement of revenue realisation and

THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SURESH PRABHU): (a) to (d) 
According to the formula for sharing of power from Central Sector Power 
Stations, power was allocated among the States/UTs of a region in accordance 
with the Central Plan Assistance and actual energy consumption in the State of 
the region for previous five years, the two factors being given equal weightage.

3234. SHRI RUMANDLA RAMACHANDRA1AH: Will the Minister of 
COAL AND MINES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Union Government has liberalised its coal policy and has 
given new guidelines recently; 
(b) if so, whether under this policy and guidelines, the State Government 
companies can now mine for coal and liginite through memorandum of article 
of association; 
(c) whether any restriction have been imposed on the companies in this 
regard; 
(d) if so,' the details thereof; and 
(e) to what extent the State Government have welcomed this move? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL AND MINES 
(SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD): (a) to (e) Yes, Sir. A revised Coal Mining 
Policy has been issued on 12th December, 2001. Under the revised policy, the 
50 

[24 April, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
State Government companies or undertakings are allowed to do mining of 
coking and non-coking coal or lignite reserves, either by opencast or 
underground method, anywhere in the country, subject to the following 
conditions: 
i)  The State Government company or undertaking (referred to as 
the 'company' hereafter) is authorised to do coal or lignite mining 
by its Memorandum and Articles of Association. 
ii) The company will do coal or lignite mining in accordance with 
the provisions of the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973, the 
Mines & Minerals (Development & Regulation) Act, 1957, the 
Contract Labour (Regulation & Abolition) Act, 1970, and all other 
mineral, environmental and labour laws and other regulations 
governing the Indian coal industry. 
iii) For coal, the company shall obtain a certificate from Coal India 
Limited to the effect that the later has no plan or willingness to 
undertake mining operations for coal in the concerned area. For 
lignite, the company shall obtain a certificate from Ney veli Lignite 
Corporation. 
iv) The proposed mining area has not been altotted to a captive mining 
compnay under the provisions of Section 3(3)(a)(iii) of the Coal 
Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973. 
v) No financial assistance from the Central Government or Coal 
India Limited or Neyveli Lignite Corporation shall be provided 
to the compnay for coal or lignite mining in the concerned area. 
vi) None of the coal or lignite mines operated by the company will 
be taken over by the Central Government or Coal India Limited 
or Neyveli Lignite Corporation in the event of closure of such a 
mine or otherwise. 
vii) No employee of the company, engaged in a coal or lignite mine 
operated by it, will be absorbed in Coal India Limited or Neyveli 
Lignite Corporation at any point of time. 
No reaction from any State Government has been received on the revised 
policy.

Statement 
Common Minimum Programme on Power 
The political parties signatory to this declaration agree on the following 
Common Minimum Programme on Power: 
• Every Indian has a right to uninterrupted and quality power supply at 
affordable rates. 
• The work of extending electrification needs to be accelerated so as to 
complete: 
. i) Electrification of all villages by the end of 10th Plan, 2007. 
ii) All households by the end of 11th Plan, 2012. 
• State Governments cannot afford to supply free power. 
— Electricity rates may be determined by independent Regulatory 
Commissions. 
 ----  Power supply may be given at subsidised rates to targeted groups 
only to the extent that the State Governments can afford to 
provide subsidies through the Budget for this purpose. 
• The real problem of management and the challenge of power sector 
reforms lies in the distribution sector where: 
a. All consumers need to be metered. 
b. Power theft has attained alarming proportions. Immediate steps 
need to be taken to eliminate theft. 
c. Technical losses need to be reduced. 
d. Energy audit arid accountability at the local level have to be 
ensured. 
e. Commercial viability needs to be achieved in the next 2-3 years 
through any or all of the following: 
—  Creating Profit Centres with full accountability 
—  Handing over of local distribution to Panchayats/Local Bodies/ 
Franchisees/Users Associations, wherever necessary 
—  Privatisation of distribution 
—  Or any other means. 
88 

[24 April, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
• State Governments may evolve their own path of reforms to suit their 
specific conditions. 
• Only commercially viable distri bution can sustain and attract the 
investments required in the sector. 
• Public sector investment in the Centre as well as in the States may be 
stepped up to ensure that in the 10th Plan the country is free of power 
shortages. This is critical for the Indian economy in the new globalised 
environment. 
• An effective programme for conserving energy through energy efficient 
lighting, pump sets and other equipment needs to be implemented 
with urgency. 
• Power sector is in a critical situation and reforms need to be undertaken 
to achieve the above objectives . Power sector reforms to be 
depoliticised in order to facilitate their speedy implementation.

Power theft 
† 3288. SHRIMATI SAVITA SHARDA: Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact.-that theft of power is still taking place in Delhi 
and the entire country des'pite change in meter policy; 
(b) if so, whether Government propose to take steps to check this; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefore? . 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER 
(SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) Yes, Sir. Theft of power takes place 
in varying magnitude in the country. Power distribution falls under the 
jurisdiction of State Governments and the activities to contain theft of power 
have to be undertaken by the power utilities. 
(b) and (c) The Central Government has given priority to reduction of 
transmission and distribution losses including power theft. The Central 
Electricity Authority has issued guidelines for reduction of transmission and 
distribution losses including power theft and for conducting Energy Audits in 
power systems. These guidelines have been circulated to all the power utilities, 
which are taking the following steps to prevent the theft of energy— 
a. Mass checking drive is carried out periodically by vigilance squads 
as well as field staff. Inspections are being carried out by district 
units of engineers and prosecutions of erring consumers are launched 
by Police Officers manning the anti Power theft Squads. 
b. Installations are being made pilfer proof. 
c. A scheme for incentive to informants is in operation. A scheme to 
recognize the performance of individuals to curb theft of energy by 
providing incentive to deserving officers/employees has also been 
introduced. 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
94 

[24 April, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
d. Load inspection studies for major load centres are being conducted. 
e. Penalty for imprisonment is also being imposed on the culprits. 
f. With the help of computerization of billing process, abnormal 
consumption of consumers is being detected. If consumption is less 
than 15% of the average, case s arc immediately inspected for 
detecting tampering of meter/theft of energy. 
The Government of India has also launched a scheme for Accelerated 
Power Development Programme for renovation & modernization/life extension 
uprating of existing old power plants, and upgradation of sub-transmission & 
distribution network including energy audit activities and metering in the 
distribution circles in a phased manner. In the first phase of this programme, 
since rechristencd as Accelerated Power Development and Reform Programme 
(APDRP), 63 distribution circles in the States have been taken up for intensive 
upgradation so as to serve as models for remaining circles in the country for 
improvement in a phased manner. The Government has made an allocation of 
Rs. 3500 crores during 2002-03. 
The Government of India had al so set up a Steering Committee for 
preparing guidelines/manuals for improvement of Sub-transmission & 
distribution systems on a scientific basis. These include guidelines on Energy 
Accounting and audit, which would help in containing commercial losses. 
Necessary amendments have been enacted to the IE Act, 1910 to make 
theft of electricity a cognizable offence.  Stricter provisions and penalties are 
envisaged in the Electricity Bill, 2001 in case of power theft.

New policy to promote FDI in Hydro Power Sector 
3290. SHRI SATISH PRADHAN: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether Government is considering any new policy to promote foreign 
direct investment in hydro power generation sector by discouraging generation 
of costly power which is generated through the utilization of various petro 
products in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER 
(SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) to (c) The Government had 
formulated a policy in 1991 to encour age greater investment by the private 
sector in the power sector. Keeping in view the growing demand for power in 
the country and the need for more investment in this sector, the Government 
of India, as part of further liberalization of the Foreign Direct Investment 
regime, has on June 12, 2000, decided to remove the upper limit for foreign 
direct investment in respect of pr ojects relating to electric generation, 
transmission and distribution(other than atomic reactor plants). 
The use of certain liquid hydro carbon liquid fuels for generation of 
electricity was permitted under the liquid fuel policy announced in 
96 

[24 April, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
November, 1995 considering the shorter gestation period of liquid fuel based 
power projects as compared to thermal power projects and the need to have a 
quick capacity addition to avert a severe power crisis. Due to the spurt in 
international prices, naphtha is no longer considered a viable fuel for generation 
of electricity, also considering the difficulty in its handling. The State Governments 
are also now reluctant to encourage naphtha based power generation. 
In order to accelerate the pace of hydro power development in the country, 
a Policy of Hydro Power Development was announced in August 1998. A 
favourable environment has been created to promote private sector investment 
in the field of hydro electric projects. The procedure for transfer of clearances 
have been streamlined and tariff rationalization have made such projects 
attractive. The Ranking St udy recently carried out by the Central Electricity 
Authority (CEA) to create a shelf of feasible projects would facilitate the hydro 
developers to take up the implementation of potential sites in a phased manner 
in order of their ranking. CEA is also in the process of formulating a National 
Action Plan in consultation with the State Governments to harness the entire 
balance potential in the country.

alia, emphasized that the hands of the PSUs should be strengthened to augment

the country's energy programme. One of  the suggestions made was that the 
PSUs may be helped to recover their dues from the State entities. It has been 
the Government's constant endeavour to asist the Central Public Sector 
Undertakings of power and coal to recover their outstanding dues from the 
State Electricity Boards (SEBs). The is sue of outstanding dues of the State 
Electricity Boards (SEBs) payable to the Central Public Sector Undertaking 
(CPSUs) was discussed in the conferen ce of Chief Ministers/Power Ministers 
in March, 2001. 
On the basis of the resolution passed in the Conference an Expert Group 
was set up under the Chairmanship of Shri Montek Singh Ahluwalia, former 
Member (Energy), Planning Commission, to: 
(i) Recommend Measures for one time settlement of outstanding dues 
of the State Electricity Boards to wards the Central Public Sector 
Undertakings as also the dues fr om the CPSUs to the State Power 
Utilities; and 
(ii) Suggest a strategy for capital re structuring of the State Electricity 
Boards including the provision of Structural Adjustment Loans so as 
to enable them to tide over the present financial crisis, make them 
operationally viable and improve their credit-rating. 
The recommendations of the Gr oup were accepted with minor 
modifications by the High Level Empowered Group of Chief Ministers. The 
modified scheme for one-time settlement  of outstanding dues was approved 
by the Government recently. The salient features of the scheme are: 
(a) The scheme would come into force from the date of issue of order or 
from the date when the State Government sign the tripartite agreement 
(with the Ministry of Finance in the Government of India and the 
Reserve Bank of India), whichever is later. 
(b) For the States participating in the scheme, 60% of the interest/surcharge 
on the delayed payments as on 30.09.2001 would be waived off. 
(c) The rest of the dues amounting to the full principal amount as well 
as the remaining 40% of the interest/surcharge would be securitised 
through bonds issue by the respective State Governments. 
(d) The bonds would be issued through RBI at a tax-free interest rate 
of 8.5% per annum. The terms of bonds should be structured to 
achieve a moratorium of 5 years on repayment of principal 
99 

RAJYA SABHA [24 April, 2002] 
with the entire principal being repaid between the 6th and 15th 
year. These bonds would be identical to bonds issued in connection 
with the market borrowings of State Governments, with the 
attendant discipline in repayments. The bonds will be subject to 
Iock-in restrictions that will allow release of only 10 per cent of the 
bonds in the secondary market each year. 
(e) Forensuring timely payment of current dues in future, defaults in 
current payment for power/fuel would attract a graded reduction in 
the supply of power from central  power stations and in coal 
supplies. Where such defaults ex ceed 90 days from the date of 
billing, the Ministry of Finance shall recover these dues through 
adjustment against releases due to them from the Centre. 
(f) In order to initiate steps toward s reform of the sector, the State 
Governments/SEBs shall accept reform-based performance 
milestones such as setting up of SERCs, metering of distribution 
feeders, improvement in revenue realisation and other such 
milestones specified in the MoUs signed/to be signed with the 
Ministry of Power. 
(g) The States shall be offered incentives for complying with the 
scheme. If SEBs or their successor entities (other than the ones not 
owned by the State Government) do not default on their current 
dues and adhere to the performance milestones, CPSUs shall pay 
them, during the first year commencing from 1.10.2001, bi-annual 
cash incentives equal to 3 per cent of the value of bonds in the first 
year, 2.5% in the second year and 2% in the third and fourth years. 
Further, if SEBs open and mainta in Letters of Credit (LCs) till the 
end of December 2002, CPSUs shall pay them a one-time cash 
incentive equal to 2 per cent of the value of bonds. In addition, 
States undertaking reforms s h a l l  also be assisted through 
Accelerated Power Development and Reform Programme 
(APRDP) grants and discretionary allocation of Power. The

Monitoring schemes by the Ministry of Rural Development 
3297. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister 
of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has introduced a new initiative to monitor 
implementation of its schemes; 
(b) if so, the details of such initiatives; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that responsibilities of area officers have 
been streamlined; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI M. 
VENKAIAH NAIDU): (a) and (b) A new initiative has been taken to 
strengthen the Monitoring and quality of implementation of Programmes of 
the Ministry by introducing a scheme of District Level Monitoring on pilot 
basis during 2001-02, with the objectives of (i) maintaining the flow of 
timely, authentic and reliable information about the performance of the 
programmes of the Ministry from the District level to the Ministry, (ii) 
obtaining qualitative feedback about the implementation and policy 
environment at the District level, and (iii) to check and verify the physical 
achievements. 
(c) and (d) The Ministry have an Area Officers Scheme, in which all 
Officers of the rank of Deputy Secretary and above have been appointed Area 
Officers for one or more States. The sc heme has been streamlined recently to 
make it more effective. The Area Office rs are required to visit the allocated 
State(s) regularly, with briefs regard ing outstanding issues and details of 
proposals for clearance and release of funds under various Programmes. The 
Area Officers are also required to'visit the DRDAs and the State Headquarters 
(in addition to the selected villages) and help to expedite submission of 
proposals. In addition, they will find out the status of implementation of the 4-
point programme and assess the impact of awareness generation programmes 
through electronic and print media, th e Area Officers are also required to 
review the programme implementation and undertake physical verification of 
the assets created.

3308. SHRIYADLAPATIVENKATRAO: Will the Minister of RURAL

(a) whether it is a fact that Government propose to link the release of

(b) if so, whether State Government have been consulted in this regard; 
and

NAIDU): (a) to (c) No. Sir. Article 243-G of the Constitution has vested the 
State Legislatures with powers to make laws to endow the Panchayats with 
118

such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as

in the Saurashtra-Kutch area of Gujarat are getting water through tankers;

the year 2000 and 2001, Rs. 32.56 crore and Rs. 36.89 crore respectively were 
spent on mitigation of drinking water scar city in Saurashtra-Kutch region. In 
the current year Rs. 3.49 crores have been spent so far for this purpose.

3312.   SHRI YADLAPATI VENKAT RAO: 
SHRI RUMANDLA RAMACHANDRAIAH: 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there has been a steep dec line in the export of rcadymade 
garments from India during the last six months; 
(b) if so, the extent of decline during this period as compared to export 
in corresponding months last year; and 
(c) the steps being taken to increase exports? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES (SHRI 
V. DHANANJAY KUMAR): (a) and (b) As per latest available DGCI&S data, 
the exports of rcadymade garment during the last six month i.e. August-January 
2001 -02 amounted to US$ 2506.7 million as against the exports of US$ 2589.0 
million during the same period of 2000-01, recording a negative growth of 
3.2%. 
(c) The various export facilitie s extended by the Government inter-alia 
to.garment exporters include duty drawback, concessional rate of duty for 
import of machineries under EPCG Scheme, allowing import of restricted items 
under the Advance Licence Scheme of the Export-Import Policy, duty free 
import of essential items of trimmings and embellishments like fastners, 
polywadding, labels, tags, buttons, hangers, stickers, polybags and lining and 
interlining materials, full/partial exemption under 80HHC of Income Tax. 
Government have also been taking several steps from time to time to 
strengthen and promote textile export s including rcadymade garments. Some 
of the important initiatives are:— 
(i) The Government has de-reserved the woven segment of rcadymade 
garment from the SSI sector. It has also announced the de-reserved 
of knitted segment in the Budget 2002-03. 
(ii) The Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS) has been made 
operational from 1-4-1999 to facilitate the modernisation and 
upgradation of this sector so that it can become more competitive 
in international trade. 
122 

[24 April. 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
(in) Weaving, processing and garment machinery, which are covered 
under TUFS, have been extend ed the facility of accelerated 
depreciation at the rate of 50%. Cost of machinery has also been 
reduced through Fiscal Policy measures. 
(iv) With a view to encouraging backward integration, the custom duty 
on shuttleless looms has been brought to 5%. A programme has 
also been announced to induct 50,000 shuttleless looms and to 
modernise 2.5 lakh powerlooms in the decentralised sector by 2004. 
(v) Foreign equity participation upto 100% through automatic route has 
been allowed in the textile sector with a few exceptions. 
(vi) National Institute for Fashion Technology (N1FT), its six branches 
and Apparel Training and Design Centres (ATDCs) are running 
various courses/programmes to meet skilled manpower requirements 
of textile industry especially apparel in the field of design, 
merchandising and marketing. 
(vii) To prepare and sensitise the textile industry to conform to the 
ecological requirements of importing countries by providing 
facilities by way of eco-testing laboratories.

to state:

capable of producing world class state-of-the-art material;

strong and vibrant industry capable of producing good quality cloth at

Waiving off the loans of weavers 
t33!4. SHRI RAM NATH  KOVIND: Will the Mi nister of TEXTILES 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government had started the weavers loan relief scheme in 
the year 1990 with a view to waiving off the loans to the tune of Rs. 10,000/-
outstanding upto 1989 to be implemented by the State Cooperative Banks; 
(b) whether the loans of the weavers belonging to all the cooperative 
weavers committees have been waived off by the Magadh Central Cooperative 
Bank in Jehanabad but loans of the weavers of Gaya district have not waived 
off till date; 
(c) whether some MPs and the Weavers Association of Gaya have drawn 
the Government's attention towards this; and 
(d) if so, the steps taken by Government in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES (SHRI 
V. DHAN ANJAY KUMAR); (a) Government of India had formulated a scheme 
known as "Agricultural and Rural Debt Relief Scheme 1990" (ARDRS) which 
was in force during the period from 15th May, 1990 to 31st March, 1991. 
Under the Scheme, the non-wilful defaults of Farmers, Land-less Labourers, 
Artisans and Weavers in rural areas to Public Sector Banks and Regional Rural 
Banks in respect of loans up to Rs. 10,000/- from these banks on or after 1st 
April, 1986, and instalments of term loans falling due after 2nd October, 1986 
which were over due to banks as on the effective date of 2nd October, 1989 
including overdue interest were written off. The liability was borne by 
Government of India. In the case of Cooperative Banks, a similar scheme was 
formulated by the State Governments on the lines of Government of India 
Scheme. The liabilities arising out of the State Scheme were shared by 
Government of India and the concerned State Governments in equal 
proportion. In the case of weavers' societies where wages and/or yam had been 
provided as advance to the members su ch wages were considered as loans 
under the scheme and were eligible for relief under the scheme provided those 
satisfied the criteria for eligibility.

within the stipulated time limit were  cleared by the Magadh District

Weavers' Cooperative Societies in Jehanabad District. However, the claims of 
Manpur Block of Gaya District were not considered, as the same were not

(c) Yes, Sir. 
(d) The scheme to waive the loans up to Rs. 10,000/- was under 
implementation for a particular period. The scheme has been discontinued

Providing yam to handloom weavers in A.P. 
3321. DR. DASARI NARAYANA RAO: Will the Minister of 
TEXTILES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have taken any concrete steps to provide yam 
to handloom weavers of Andhra Pradesh at affordable rates and in sufficient 
quantities; and 
(b) if so, details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OFTEXTILES (SHRI 
V. DHANANJAY KUMAR): (a) Yes, Sir. The Government of India has been 
implementing a scheme for arranging supply of yam to handloom weavers, at 
the prices at which it is available at the mill gate. This scheme is 
implemented throughout  the country. 
(b) The aforesaid scheme is im plemented through the National 
Handloom Development Corporation Ltd. (NHDC), a Central Public Sector 
Undertaking. Under the scheme NHDC makes available all types of yam 
required by handloom weavers and their organizations against indents, at the 
price at which the yarn is available at the mill gate i.e. the place of 
manufacturing. Hence, the weavers do  not have to bear the cost of 
transportation from the spinning mills. Thus, the yam becomes generally 
more affordable than if purchased from the local market. Under the scheme, 
NHDC has supplied 55.68 lakh kg yam worth Rs. 6265.40 lakh in Andhra 
Pradesh in the years 1995-96 to 2001-02 (up to February, 2002.)

and has been done from time to time.

have been taken: 
• formulation of new schemes namely, Apparel Parks for Exports Scheme

decentralized powerloom industry; 
• Policy changes, namely, dereservation of the garment sector, raising of 
SSI limit of investment in knitwear industry to Rs. 5 crore; 
• Changes and concessions in the duty and tariff structures to support 
modernization and growth and investment, announced in the budget;

RE. COMMEMORATION OF THE CENTENARY YEAR OF 
ANUSHILAN SAMITI 
Matter raised with permission of the Chair 
. MR. CHAIRMAN: Shri Manoj Bhattacharya. 
SHRI MANOJ BHATTACHARYA (West Bengal): Sir, the Anushilan 
Samiti, the organisation of the devout revolutionary freedom fighters of our 
country, was formed in a meeting on 23 rd and 24 th March, 1902, in Calcutta, 
the then epicentre of revolutionary armed struggle against the inhuman British 
rule. 
156 

[24 APRIL, 2002] RAJYA SABHA  
This is the centenar y year of this great organisation, which 
contributed immensely to the freedom st ruggle of ours and fought relentlessly 
against the most brutal atrocities of tyrannical imperialism. This organisation 
was founded by none other than Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das, Sri Arobinda 
(Ghosh), Pramatha Nath Mitra, Surendranath Banerjee and others. 
Sir, the Anushilan Samiti was the pioneer organisation which could 
consciously promote revolutionism a nd emancipation of the common people 
from the yoke of subhuman socio-econ omic and political situation under the 
British colonial rule. Against all possible and impossible odds, the organisation 
could garner formidable strength in entire Northern India and Maharashtra, 
through the Gadar Party, the Hindustan Republican Army, later the Hindustan 
Socialist Republican Army of the great Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, 
Chandrasekhar Azad, Ramprasad Bismil, Asfaqulla, et al., who laid down their 
precious lives for our dear nation. We  can never forget the chanting of 
'Inquilab Zindabad' by the great martyr Bhagat Singh. The great 
revolutionaries of Uttar Pradesh, to name a few Jogesh Chatterjee, Rajen 
Lahiri and Jatin Das, Maharaj Trailokaya Chakaraborty, Masterda Surya Sen, 
Pulin Das. et al. of Bengal were very actively involved in building this 
organisation. This organisation, way back during the first decade of the last 
century, gave a clarion call for emanc ipation of the peasants and toiling 
millions, through mass actions against colonialism. 
We must remember that the founder  of the great Indian National 
Army, the Azad Hind Fauj, that led the armed action against the British rule, 
was none other than the legendary Rashbehari Bose who had been the main 
organiser of the Anushilan Samiti for a long time before he was forced to 
choose a life in exile. In fact, the revolutionary upheaval against the tyranny of 
colonialism shook the entire British Empire. Thousands of brave young men 
and women sacrificed their lives, unsung and unwept. Many consciously 
concealed their identity even before thei r death for the noble cause of their 
ideals. The dreams of these great patrio ts could not be realised even till this 
day. Their lives were their ideals and those are worth emulating, particularly, at 
this hour of national crisis, when t he most dreaded force of communalism is 
out with its fangs open in Gujarat an d elsewhere, the most ugly divisive 
terrorist forces are haunting the entire  nation, particularly, in Jammu and 
Kashmir and in the North-Eastern States. 
Sir, I, on behalf of my party, the Revolutionary Socialist Party, urge 
upon the Government of India to commemorate the centenary year of the 
157 

RAJYA SABHA [24 APRIL, 2002]  
Anushilan Samiti with gaiety, and immediately release a commemorative 
postal stamp on this auspicious occasion. 
SHRI T.N. CHATURVEDI (Uttar Pradesh): Sir, I rise to associate myself with the 
Special Mention of my hon. colleague. The Anushilan Samiti spread the 
revolutionary movement in the country. The heroes of this body have carved out a 
niche for themselves in the history and it is time for us to remember them and issue 
a commemoration. It will be a great inspiration for the generations to come.

Steep Hike in Passport Fee 
SHRI M.P. ABDUSSAMAD SAMADANI (Kerala): Sir, I draw the 
attention of the House to a situation created by the increase in the passport 
fee. The sudden and large increase in the fee for the issuance of the passport 
has dealt a serious blow to the numberless job-seeking young people of the 
country. People are compelled to go abroad mainly for job opportunities. The 
majority of the people travel to the fo reign countries, not for sight-seeing and 
tourism. They leave their families, paren ts and children, in search of some 
employment for their sustenance. The Government's decision to increase the 
passport fee has somehow burdened the unemployed citizens of the country. 
The majority of the people travel abroad because of the serious unemployment 
problem here. The Government is not abl e to provide job opportunities for its 
young generation. What right such a Government has to exploit the poor 
unemployed citizens who intend to go abroad seeking a path for their 
livelihood? Most of those who travel abroad for employment belong to the 
middle class and the poorest sections of  the society. The numberless families 
are living in our country and they depend upon the income from their members 
who work abroad. Why is the Governm ent closing this door of seeking job 
opportunities for its own citizens? It is  nothing but cruel. Those Indians who 
work abroad contribute to a great extent to the national exchequer, through 
foreign exchange. It is not fair to harass them by every means; some times by 
an increase in the

Protection of material evidence 
SHRI K. B. KRISHNA MURTHY (K arnataka): Mr. Chairman, Sir, I 
wish to state the dispensation of crim inal justice in our country has reached a 
dismal level. The conviction rates in our criminal courts are only 6 per cent. My 
focus in today's Special Mention is with regard to the criminal trial of dons and 
kingpins of organised crime, who thrive on a criminal network and when they 
are arrested for heinous offences and pu t to criminal trial the prosecution 
witnesses are terrorised by the associates of the accused and the witness 
turns hostile and the accused is acquitted. 
159 

RAJYA SABHA [24 APRIL, 2002]  
My suggestion to the Government is that it enacts special laws, which 
may be used in rare cases when the State is prosecuting dangerous criminals. 
I would suggest that this law be called the Protection of Material Evidence Act. 
The legislative intent of this Act would be that in sensitive cases the 
Government should identify important prosecution witness and if in their 
opinion a conviction can be recorded on his testimony by the court of law, he 
should be taken into protective custody before the trial and be given necessary 
protection so that he may truthfully depose in the court without being subject to 
coercion, duress and after the material  witness delivers the testimony he 
should be given protection for a prescribed period, to save him from any 
retribution by the accused or his associates. It is my profound hope that if 
protection is given to a material witness pre and post criminal trial, the ends of 
justice can be met. Thank you.

Indian Railways are the lifeline of the nation. They have been prime 
movers to the economy and the society of the Indian sub-continent. It has the 
distinction and pride of being one of the largest railway systems in the world. In 
the process, Railways have become the symbol of our integration and strategic

stations. It is transporting about 30 m illion passengers and more than one MT 
of freight daily with the help of 1.5 million employees. The assets of the
